subject: Why the marker name is not shown from scanone summary

messages.author: 82933c06b1097cc4
messages.subject: Why the marker name is not shown from scanone summary
parts:
Hi all,
I recently analyzed a set of data by rqtl, after scanone I used the below command
np_scan1_ril_D14_28_hk<-summary(scan1_ril_D_14_28_hk,perms=perm_scan1_ril_D14_28_hk,alpha=0.05)
And Then np_scan1_ril_D14_28_hk
But I got

                         chr   pos  lod
c3.loc3                    3  8.73 3.74
P_2517957   5 50.16 3.29


So my question is: Why I got c3.loc 3 instead of the marker name? (There is no marker at pos 8.73, there's one at pos5 and one at pos 14). Besides, How is the loc 3 inferred?
Thank you so much
Gill

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Why the marker name is not shown from scanone summary
parts:
Calculations are performed at the markers and also at "pseudomarker" positions between markers (as defined by the step argument in calc.genoprob). The pseudomarkers are assigned names like c3.loc3.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Why the marker name is not shown from scanone summary
parts:
fill.geno() does imputations.

pull.geno() will just pull out whatever is there, with NAs as in the data.

karl
